properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised by Anthony asking how CI and regression testing here could be improved, 2026-09-21.

THE OBSERVATION. `ci.yml` runs roughly 48 gates. Several carry a comment saying the author personally proved the gate fails before trusting it — "shown to fail on an argument-leak mutation before it was trusted", "verified to FAIL on all three drift shapes before being wired here, not merely to pass on a clean tree", "MUTATION-CHECKED five ways". That discipline is real and it is being practised carefully. It is also PER-AUTHOR, PER-GATE, ONE TIME, AND IN PROSE: nothing re-runs it, so a gate that silently stops being able to fail — a moved file, a changed exit code, a filter that now matches nothing — goes on reporting green forever, and green is the reading nobody questions.

Two gates already answer this for themselves, and they are the proof the idea is buildable: `replies_are_bounded.py` and `a_reply_is_sent_once.py` both FAIL IF THEY MEASURED NOTHING, on the explicit ground that "no tool overflowed" and "I could not make any tool overflow" must not share an exit code. The question is whether that property belongs to two gates or to all of them.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A META-GATE that, for each gate, applies a known-bad mutation to a scratch tree and requires a non-zero exit. Strongest and by far the most expensive: it needs one seeded defect per gate, hand-written, and those seeds rot.
(b) THE CHEAP SUBSET — require only that every gate exits non-zero on an EMPTY or NONSENSE input (no files matched, empty design, missing export). This catches the specific failure the gate runner's own docstring records — a first draft that "exited 0 on a filter that matched nothing" — and costs one generic harness rather than 48 seeds.
(c) A CONVENTION ONLY: every new gate must ship its own hermetic suite. This is already the house practice (nine `test_*.py` gates exist purely to net other gates), so the honest version of (c) is to make it a stated rule with a lint, not a new instrument.
(d) NOTHING — the prose comments are the record, and a mechanised version buys less than it costs.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is not weak: this is a gate on gates, which is exactly the shape of over-engineering Anthony names. (b) is defensible because it is one harness for a whole class; (a) is 48 hand-written seeds that will drift and is probably the version to decline.
properties.name: OPEN — should the build itself prove each of its ~48 gates can go RED, instead of each author proving it once by hand in a comment?
properties.rationale: Recorded open because the cheap form and the expensive form differ by an order of magnitude in cost and the design has no measurement saying which class of gate failure actually happens here. The one measured instance — a runner exiting 0 having run nothing — is caught by (b), which is an argument for the cheap form and against the thorough one.
